items.title: Google releases March 2026 spam update
items.summary: Google released its March 2026 spam update on March 24, 2026, describing it as a standard spam update rolling out across all languages and locations, which may take only a few days to complete. This is the first spam update of 2026, following the August 2025 spam update, and could lead to ranking or traffic changes due to its focus on improving spam detection systems like SpamBrain. Sites affected should review Google's spam policies to ensure compliance, as changes may help improve rankings over time.

items.title: Ross Simmonds on AI SEO: AEO and GEO Beyond Traditional SEO
items.summary: Ross Simmonds discusses a podcast with Mike King (@iPullRank) on AI and SEO, warning that viewing AEO and GEO as mere rebrands of SEO risks losing relevance. AI discovery uses retrieval augmented generation and evaluates content ecosystems like Reddit and YouTube, not just sites. Marketers must map synthetic queries and build matching ecosystems.

items.title: The Rise of GEO: SEO’s New Frontier + Free 2026 GEO Checklist
items.summary: M. Rock Stone argues SEO is dying with organic traffic down and AI slashing CTRs, positioning GEO as key to AI citations. New signals: brand voice, conversational intent, schema; tips include conversational rewrites, original research, no AI crawler blocks. Free checklist offered in linked article.

items.title: AEO and GEO: The New SEO Debate
items.summary: Asteris highlights AEO and GEO as the emerging debate in SEO, shifting from blue links to AI answers. Brand visibility now hinges on AI models trusting your content over traditional rankings. This reflects evolving discovery in AI-driven search.

items.title: Horror Novel Pulled by Publishers Over Alleged AI Use
items.summary: The US release of horror novel 'Shy Girl' by Mia Ballard was cancelled by its publisher amid concerns over AI assistance in writing. The book had already been published in the UK. Ballard attributes any AI involvement to an editor hired for her self-published version.

items.title: A.I. Is Writing Fiction. Publishers Are Unprepared
items.summary: Publishers face challenges as AI-generated fiction enters the market, highlighted by recent controversies like the 'Shy Girl' cancellation. Industry consultant Thad McIlroy warns that clarifying AI policies is inevitable. The article discusses broader implications for the publishing industry.

items.title: Writers Accused of AI Use Because LLMs Trained on Their Books
items.summary: Author J.A. Konrath notes that LLMs pirated over 80 of his books and now mimic his style, leading to accusations of him using AI. Features like Oxford commas and em-dashes, long used by him, are flagged as AI signs. He questions if other pirated authors face similar issues.

items.title: AI Contamination Spreads to Physical Books, Hurting Human Writers
items.summary: User Dickie Dogfather laments AI-generated books flooding physical markets, forcing human writers to compete with minimal-effort ChatGPT outputs. He earns modestly from writing and views this as a profound threat. The post highlights frustration with AI in children's books like those on the Punic Wars.

items.title: Challenges in Training AI for Creative Writing
items.summary: Anthropologist Jasmine Sun discusses why AIs excel in math and coding but struggle with creative writing, producing only 'okay poem' level output. She interviewed AI trainers for The Atlantic on the difficulties. The post shares images and links to the article.

items.title: 98th Academy Awards Winners Announced
items.summary: The 98th Oscars ceremony occurred on March 15, 2026, at the Dolby Theatre, honoring top films. 'One Battle After Another' won Best Picture, Best Director, Best Supporting Actor for Sean Penn, and three other awards. Other highlights included acting wins for Jessie Buckley and Michael B. Jordan, with notable red carpet arrivals and performances.

items.title: Sean Penn Wins Best Supporting Actor but Skips Oscars for Ukraine
items.summary: Sean Penn received the Best Supporting Actor Oscar for his role but chose to travel to Ukraine instead of attending the ceremony. This decision highlights his ongoing activism amid the awards night's glamour. Coverage noted complete Oscars highlights and winners.

items.title: Disney's Tangled Reboot Casting Sparks Interest Over Milo Manheim's Backstory
items.summary: Disney announced Milo Manheim, son of a gay dad and Camryn Manheim, as the lead in the live-action Tangled reboot. The casting comes after years of audience backlash to perceived woke elements in Disney projects. Observers note it may test audience reactions again.

items.title: Oscars Slammed for 'Virtue Signaling' Speeches by Woke Hollywood
items.summary: A video clip from the 2026 Oscars shows filmmakers making political statements about government murders and media oligarchs during acceptance speeches. Online users criticized it as endless virtue signaling from woke Hollywood elites. The moment contributed to broader backlash against the ceremony's tone.

items.title: Hollywood Elites Leave Oscars Venue in Trash Amid Climate Lectures
items.summary: A photo reveals the Dolby Theatre littered with plastic bottles, wrappers, and debris right after the Oscars on March 16, 2026. Critics pointed out the hypocrisy of celebrities who preached environmentalism and plastic bans during the event. The image went viral highlighting elite disconnect.

items.title: Oscars Celebrate Woke Flops as Hollywood Declines
items.summary: A cartoon post depicts Hollywood's Oscars as out of touch, praising woke films like Snow White, a $170M flop blamed on Rachel Zegler and CGI dwarfs. It notes 50% drop in productions, 40% box office crash, and low ratings amid anti-Trump preaching. Audiences expressed frustration with the industry's direction.

items.title: AI may be helping more people start their own businesses, but without many employees
items.summary: AI is enabling more people to start businesses solo by handling tasks traditionally done by teams, leading to smaller startups with lower costs and rapid scaling. Companies like Block are leveraging AI advancements to restructure, laying off staff while boosting efficiency, as noted by Jack Dorsey. Examples such as TurboAI illustrate how one technical employee can now manage workloads previously requiring multiple roles, transforming entrepreneurship.

items.title: Durable AI Builds Entire Small Businesses in Minutes with Websites, CRM, and Customer Agents
items.summary: Durable has launched an advanced AI tool that creates a complete small business setup in minutes, including website, branding, SEO optimization, domain, CRM, payments, and revenue strategies. It further deploys AI agents to attract customers autonomously while owners sleep. With over 3 million users, it's challenging high-cost agencies charging $10k for basic websites.

items.title: Free 338-Page AI Playbook for Small Businesses to Drive Real Impact
items.summary: Austen Allred released a comprehensive 338-page AI playbook generated by Claude AI, designed specifically for small business owners to integrate AI effectively. The guide features detailed, research-backed strategies divided into actionable sections. It's available for free download, helping non-tech-savvy businesses maximize AI benefits.
